# The NPDev Manager, in plain words

*[Português](MANAGER_GUIDE.pt.md)*

**For:** someone who wants to build an app with NPDev and has never written Java, Python or SQL.
You do not need to know what those are. This guide tells you what each thing is *for*, so you know
what you are installing and why.

NPDev builds web applications from a description. You describe your app (what it keeps, who may do
what); NPDev writes, builds and runs the program. The **NPDev Manager** is the window where you do
all of it, without a terminal.

In a hurry? Go straight to [Your first app in 10 minutes](FIRST_APP_IN_10_MINUTES.md).

## The four places

The bar at the top of the Manager has four places. Each one answers one question. Inside a place, a
second row lists its screens, with one line saying what the place is for.

| Place | What it is for | Screens inside |
|---|---|---|
| 🔧 **Set up** | Get this computer ready to build apps. You do this once. | Check my computer, Install what is missing |
| ▦ **My apps** | Create an app, start it, change it, share it. | All apps, Start & stop, Edit, Ask AI, Data, Share, Browser checks (checks), Data-rule checks (checks), Impact (advanced), Packs (advanced) |
| ◉ **Activity** | Everything running on this computer, at a glance. | Running apps |
| ⚙ **Settings** | AI providers, passwords, NPDev versions. You set these once. | AI providers, Passwords & keys, NPDev versions, This computer, Platform checks (advanced), AI evaluations (advanced) |

## Five paths through the Manager

1. **The first time.** **Set up › Check my computer**, then **Set up › Install what is missing**, then
   **My apps › All apps** to create an app, then **My apps › Start & stop** to start it and open it in the
   browser. This is [Your first app in 10 minutes](FIRST_APP_IN_10_MINUTES.md).
2. **Every day.** **My apps**: change the app in **My apps › Edit** or **My apps › Ask AI**,
   then start it in **My apps › Start & stop**.
3. **Show it to someone.** Check it in **My apps › Browser checks**, then **My apps › Share**.
4. **Something went wrong.** **Activity** shows every app on this computer: which is running,
   which stopped, which has a problem, and its logs.
5. **Once, then forget.** **Settings**: AI providers, passwords and keys, NPDev versions.

## What NPDev puts on your computer, and why

Everything below the first table is optional. Nothing is installed without you pressing a button,
and the private copies the Manager downloads touch nothing else on your computer.

**Installed once, needed by everything**

| What | What it is | Why it matters | If it is missing or fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Java (JDK 17)** | The engine your generated app runs on. | NPDev turns your model into a Java program. Java is what runs it, the way a music player plays a song file. | Nothing can be built or started. **Set up › Install what is missing** downloads a private copy (about 180 MB) that touches nothing else on your computer. |
| **Python** | Runs NPDev's own tools (the npdev command). | The checks, the generator launcher and the Monitor are small Python programs. You never write Python yourself. | The Manager cannot ask NPDev anything and most screens stay empty. **Set up › Install what is missing** adds a private copy only if your computer has none. |
| **NPDev and its setup** | NPDev itself, downloaded as a version, then prepared once on this computer. | Setup builds or downloads the pieces every generated app is assembled from. After that, creating an app is fast. | Apps cannot be generated, and **Set up › Check my computer** shows 'NPDev jars: not staged'. Setup usually takes about a minute, sometimes about ten; the progress lines show it is alive. |

**Where an app keeps its data (you pick one per app)**

| What | What it is | Why it matters | If it is missing or fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| **H2Local** | A small database that lives in a file next to your app. The default, and where to start. | Nothing to install, nothing to configure. Your data survives when the app stops. | Nothing to install. If it refuses to start, another copy of the same app is probably still running and holding the file. |
| **PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server** | Full database servers, the usual choice for a real deployment or for a database a company already runs. | Many people can use the app at once, and the data lives apart from the app. | Only needed if you choose one. NPDev runs them through Docker, or connects to one you already run (tick 'This server is mine' when creating the app). Use Test connection to see exactly what fails. |

**Optional: only some features need it**

| What | What it is | Why it matters | If it is missing or fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Docker** | A program that runs other programs in sealed boxes. | NPDev uses it to start a PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server database for your app without installing one. | Fine. A '!' next to Docker is expected. Choose H2Local and everything works. |
| **git** | Keeps a history of every version of your app's model. | Your model is your app. With git you can always go back to a version that worked. | Fine. The Manager does not install it and nothing needs it; your app simply has no history until you add it. |
| **Browser checks (ScrapForAI)** | A robot browser that clicks through your app to see that it still works. | It tests that a person could actually use the screens, not just that the program starts. | Optional. Without it, **My apps › Browser checks** cannot run; everything else works. |
| **Tunnel (cloudflared)** | A small program that gives this computer a temporary public web address. | So someone else can open your app for a quick demo, without renting a server. | Optional. Needed only for level 1 of **My apps › Share**, 'Shared by link'. |

## Words you will see

| What | What it is | Why it matters | If it is missing or fails |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Model** | The description of your app (the file model.json): what it keeps, who may do what, which screens exist. | You, or an AI, write the model; NPDev writes the program. The model is the part worth keeping: the program can always be generated again from it. | Every app starts from one: creating an app writes a first, working model for you. |
| **Concept** | One kind of thing your app keeps, like Customer, Order or Repair. | Each concept becomes a list screen, a form, a database table and an API, all generated. | An app with no concepts has nothing to show. |
| **Port** | The 'door number' an app answers on, as in localhost:8080. | Two programs cannot answer on the same door, so each running app needs its own. | If the app builds but will not start, the door is taken (often by an older copy of the same app). Stop it in **Activity**, or pick another port number. |
| **Access key (API key)** | The key that opens your new app, created the first time it starts. | A new app has no users yet, so someone has to be able to get in. The run log prints it once, as 'X-Api-Key: …', and keeps it in the app's secrets/api-key.env file. | Lost the log? Open secrets/api-key.env in the app's folder. The line reads NPDEV_AUTH_API_KEYS=<key>=dev:developer:admin; the key is the part between the two '=' signs. |
| **Spring Boot** | The ready-made Java framework every generated app is built on. | It gives each app a web server, sign-in and database access out of the box, so NPDev only generates what is specific to your app. | Never installed separately: it comes inside each generated app. If an error mentions Spring, the cause is usually Java, the port or the database. |
| **Gradle** | The tool that compiles your app into something that runs. | Building a Java app means compiling many files and fetching libraries. The first build downloads a lot and takes a few minutes; later ones are fast. | Comes with each app. A first build that fails while downloading is usually a network, VPN or proxy problem. |

## When something goes wrong

- **"Windows protected your PC"** when installing: expected, the Manager is not code-signed yet.
  Click *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
- **A download fails:** almost always a company network or VPN blocking GitHub. Try another network.
- **"NPDev jars: not staged"** in **Set up › Check my computer**: setup has not finished. That row's
  **Fix this** button takes you to **Set up › Install what is missing**; press **Run setup** there.
- **The app builds but will not start:** its port is taken. Change **Port** in **My apps › Start & stop**
  to another number (8081, 8090...) and press **▶ Run** again.
- **Anything else:** take a screenshot of **Activity** and of the log, and send them with the
  step you were on. "It did not work on my computer" is the most useful report there is.
